title: scheduler: latency-drift compensator for continuous-batcher to reduce starvation
author: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: This PR introduces a latency-drift compensator into the continuous-batcher scheduler. The compensator monitors per-queue running latency and recent service shortfalls, dynamically adjusts admission weights and per-request jittered timeouts, and coordinates with a light KV-cache pinning fallback to avoid long-lived starvation in co-located KV-heavy workloads. Motivation: Recent customer workloads with mixed short/long sequences exposed cases where continuous batching heuristics could allow sustained starvation of low-throughput, latency-sensitive lanes when long KV-miss requests dominate batch composition. Existing mitigations (static priority boosts, simple TTL-based preemption) reduced tail latency but caused oscillation and expensive cache thrashing. Design: The compensator implements three cooperating mechanisms: 1) Drift estimator: a running estimator per-lane that computes 'latency drift' = observed P95 - expected SLO; it uses an EWMA with bias correction to avoid overreacting to single spikes. 2) Admission rebalancer: when drift for a lane exceeds a threshold, the compensator increases that lane's admission weight by a bounded factor and schedules soft backoffs on competing lanes. Adjustments decay with an adaptive half-life proportional to current load to prevent oscillation. 3) Jittered soft-timeouts: requests from lanes with high drift receive a small randomized timeout budget (10-50ms) added to their scheduling window to prioritize completion without hard-preemptions. KV-cache pinning fallback: when a lane is identified as KV-heavy and repeatedly starved, the compensator coordinates with the KV-cache layer to pin hot keys for a short duration (configurable) to avoid repeated long fetches; pins are conservative and evicted preferentially when memory pressure increases. Telemetry & tuning: new metrics: scheduler.latency_drift{lane}, scheduler.weight_adjustment{lane}, scheduler.timeout_jitter_ms{lane}, kv_cache.pinned_keys_count, kv_cache.pin_evictions. Defaults chosen from offline benches (see bench/bench_compensator.go). Testing: unit tests for estimator/backoff logic (pkg/scheduler/compensator_test.go), integration fixture simulating KV-miss storms, and small-scale bench harness to assert non-regression on median and 95/99 latency for mixed loads. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag --enable-drift-compensator (default off), staged rollout via canary percentage and automatic rollback on regressions detected in SLO monitors. After two weeks of canary and manual verification we enabled default-on for dedicated clusters. Backwards compatibility: no API or protobuf changes. Config knobs added to runtime config and console UI for operator tuning. Related work: follows recommendations from ENG-3421 (continuous-batcher fairness review) and uses heuristics from ENG-3489 (kv pinning guidelines).

release_notes: Introduce latency-drift compensator for the continuous-batcher scheduler. Reduces prolonged starvation of latency-sensitive lanes under KV-heavy or long-sequence mixes by adaptive admission rebalancing, jittered soft-timeouts, and conservative KV-cache pinning. Metrics and operator knobs added. No public API changes.
notes_for_operators: Feature initially gated behind --enable-drift-compensator. Recommended canary: 5% traffic for 72h, monitor scheduler.latency_drift and kv_cache.pinned_keys_count. Default conservative knobs: drift_threshold_ms=40, max_weight_boost=1.5, kv_pin_duration_ms=5000, kv_pin_memory_threshold_pct=20. If kv_pin_memory_threshold_pct is exceeded, pinning is disabled until pressure subsides.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: mis-tuned expectations could over-prioritize low-volume lanes and increase overall throughput tail. Mitigations: bounded weight multipliers, adaptive decay proportional to load, opt-out flag for critical workloads, and progressive rollout with SLO-based automatic rollback. Added additional telemetry to detect oscillation and a dashboard in Redwood Console docs/design/continuous-batcher-compensator.md.
notes: Bench scripts and a small recorded workload are included in cmd/bench; see docs for how to reproduce the KV-starvation scenario.
